_title: Reopening triggers — the named capabilities whose arrival would revive a closed path
_role: THE ONE HOME FOR THE SEARCH QUERIES that detect each reopening trigger. It is NOT the one home for the route<->trigger mapping (that is research/manuscripts/emc-systems-map.json's registry rows and research/manuscripts/nr4a3-program-map.md section 6b), and it is NOT the one home for what each trigger would unlock in prose (that is research/method-watch.md's capability->action table). This file exists because those two say WHAT to watch for and neither says HOW to look for it, so nobody was looking.
_why_it_exists: CLAUDE.md section 5: 'parked items are revisit when capability X lands, not dead'. The repo already named the X for every parked row, but the weekly scan searched a fixed generic topic list that had no link to those rows, so a paper that satisfied a named trigger would have been indistinguishable from background. Each entry below turns a named trigger into runnable queries and names, from its own metadata, which routes/requirements a hit would reopen — so the scan output states the CONSEQUENCE, not just the paper.
_reconciliation: TWO ID VOCABULARIES EXIST AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME ONE — say so rather than letting a reader assume. This file's ids are TRG-*; emc-systems-map.json's revival_trigger fields (which landed the same day, independently) use TR-*. Neither is wrong and neither is being renamed under the other: that registry is the one home for WHICH ROUTE a trigger revives, this file is the one home for HOW TO SEARCH for it, and a route's revival condition is not always searchable at all (several of theirs are this repo's own work). The join is the per-trigger 'registry_trigger_ids' field below, and `python3 scripts/trigger_scan.py --check` enforces it in BOTH directions.

_registry_reconciliation.mapped_here: 10 of the registry's TR-* ids have a TRG-* counterpart, joined via each trigger's registry_trigger_ids (10 triggers carry the field).

_registry_reconciliation.divergence_worth_knowing: The registry maps RT-RIBOZYME / RT-SYNPROMOTER / RT-CRISPR-CAS13 to TR-OLIGO-TUMOUR-DELIVERY. This file splits that into TRG-OLIGO-DELIVERY-TECH (an oligonucleotide reaching the tumour) and TRG-VECTOR-DELIVERY-SOLID-TUMOUR (a vector delivering a transcriptional payload), because the registry itself carries BLK-DELIVERY and BLK-VECTOR-DELIVERY as separate blockers and the evidence that would clear one need not clear the other. Recorded rather than silently reconciled — the two files disagree about the grain, and whoever owns the registry should decide, not this file.
_registry_reconciliation.open: Nothing checks that a registry TR-* id and the TRG-* it joins to still describe the SAME capability — only that the join exists. A rewritten description on either side would pass. ⚠ AND the join is still ASYMMETRIC for three more pairs, found while repairing the E3 one on 2026-08-03 and recorded rather than unilaterally fixed, because this file does not own the registry: TR-POSE-METHODS-CONVERGE, TR-NR4A3-RXR-HETERODIMER-REPORT and TR-EMC-EXPRESSION-DATASET carry no `scan_trigger`, and emc_systems_map_check.py warns that 'nothing is searching for it' — while the last two ARE searched for here (TRG-NR4A3-DIRECT-MATTER and TRG-EMC-EXPRESSION-DATASET name them in registry_trigger_ids). The warn is therefore false in two of the three cases, and clearing it is a one-field edit in the registry by whoever owns it.
_registry_reconciliation._2026_08_03_join_repair: TRG-E3-RECRUITER-STRUCTURE had no registry_trigger_ids even though the registry's TR-E3-RECRUITER-STRUCTURE already carried scan_trigger: ['TRG-E3-RECRUITER-STRUCTURE'] — so the join existed in one direction only, for precisely the trigger that then fired first. Repaired while grading that firing. Nothing else changed.

triggers_here_with_no_registry_counterpa.TRG-FEM1B-LINKER-BEARING-STRUCTURE: Created 2026-08-03 by the grading of TRG-E3-RECRUITER-STRUCTURE's first firing. It has no TR-* counterpart because the registry's E3 trigger is scoped to the three BLOCKED recruiters and FEM1B is a gate-passer dropped on a different axis — a genuinely different capability, recorded here rather than silently widened into the registry's string. Whoever owns the registry should decide whether it wants a TR-* for it.

_integrity: A hit is an UNVALIDATED LEAD and a prompt to read the paper, never a status change and never a result. CLAUDE.md section 5's guardrail applies in full: a coming capability justifies waiting or re-running, never claiming a result before the method supports it.

_status_values.watching: not landed; the scan searches for it
_status_values.landed: the capability arrived; the paired action is owed or done — kept so a later scan does not re-raise it
_status_values.superseded: the trigger no longer describes anything we want, because the route it served changed

_trigger_kinds.external_capability: something the field has to publish/release. Searchable — this is what the scan is for.
_trigger_kinds.internal_work: the roadmap names the reopening condition as work THIS repo would do (a different frame, a different ensemble, a design change). No literature query can detect it; listed so the register is complete and nobody records it as forgotten.

triggers.title: A co-folder evaluated on ternary ASSEMBLY rather than per-chain pocket accuracy
triggers.capability: A sequence-level structure predictor whose reported benchmark is the target<->E3 INTERFACE of a ternary complex (DockQ/fnat on the induced interface), not global or per-chain accuracy. The repo's measurement is that a current co-folder can build the internal E3 machinery to near-native accuracy and still place the two halves with zero native interface contacts — so per-chain accuracy is not evidence about assembly.

reopens.also_reopens: the celastrol-C551 covalent re-fold row and, with it, the required covalent control set — both parked in the same section on 'a better co-folder or a hand-placed pose'
reopens.note: Boltz-2 failing is not the class failing; the same harness already recognises a correct ternary when one is supplied, so the plumbing is not what missed.

triggers.on_fire: Re-run the ternary rebuild by the assembly route against the new predictor and re-grade V12; do NOT read a global-accuracy number as an assembly claim — check the paper reports an interface metric on held-out ternaries.

triggers.title: A ternary generator that does not require both binding sites to be supplied
triggers.capability: A ternary/induced-complex generator that predicts the assembly from sequence + ligand alone. The one tool here that reaches a usable interface score does so only when BOTH binding sites are handed to it, which makes it a poser rather than a predictor and propagates whatever binary pose it was given.

reopens.note: A generator that needs both sites cannot be evidence that a ternary FORMS; it can only be evidence about geometry conditional on an assumed binary pose.

_query_revision.why: The first real firing returned 6 hits and NONE satisfied the criterion. Two causes, both in the query: (1) the recruiter list included KEAP1 and FEM1B, which are gate-PASSERS dropped on the Pareto front — a different question from structural stageability — and 3 of the 6 hits were KEAP1 redox pharmacology (acute lung injury, coenzyme A, heart failure) with no bearing on anything here; (2) the second clause admitted TITLE:ligand, TITLE:covalent, TITLE:degrader and TITLE:recruiter, which select for 'a ligand exists' — precisely the constraint this row already recorded as the WRONG one. The revision scopes the genes to the three the row actually blocks and requires a STRUCTURAL word.
_query_revision.superseded_query: (TITLE:RNF114 OR TITLE:DCAF16 OR TITLE:DCAF15 OR TITLE:DCAF11 OR TITLE:FEM1B OR TITLE:KEAP1) AND (TITLE:structure OR TITLE:crystal OR TITLE:"cryo-EM" OR TITLE:ligand OR TITLE:covalent OR TITLE:degrader OR TITLE:recruiter)
_query_revision.false_negative_risk_accepted: exclude_match drops titles framed as molecular glues, which is where the criterion is by construction NOT met — but a paper could in principle report a glue AND a partner-free structure and would now be missed. Accepted because decisive_evidence above makes the PDB census the real check and it is free, run on every grading, and cannot be fooled by a title.

decisive_evidence._why_this_field_exists: The 2026-08-03 grading showed the scan can only ever surface a PAPER, while this trigger's criterion is a DEPOSITED STRUCTURE. A paper is weak evidence for it and a PDB census is decisive, free and offline-checkable. Grading from the papers alone is what would have produced a wrong answer.

decisive_evidence.criterion: n_clean_binary_entries > 0 for RNF114, DCAF16 or DCAF15. Anything else is not this trigger.

hits_graded: MED/42045146 — New Reversible Covalent Warheads: Cyanobenzothiazoles Recruiting DCAF16 for Targeted Protein Degradation (J Med Chem, 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c00889)
MED/42456065 — Structure-Guided Discovery of Novel Dual-Site FEM1B Ligands and Assessment of Their Use in Targeted Protein Degradation (J Med Chem, 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c00968)
last_graded.evidence_level: Both papers are PAYWALLED — ABSTRACTS ONLY (Europe PMC fullTextXML 404, not in PMC, no preprint version indexed). The PDB census is definitive and is what the verdict rests on; the abstract reading is corroborating and labelled provisional.
last_graded.why: The DCAF16 paper is a template-assisted covalent GLUE: its own abstract says the cyanobenzothiazole, carried on the BRD4-targeting ligand, 'modifies DCAF16 at Cys58, promoting ternary complex formation'. That is the architecture the 0.3442 buried fraction already described, not a refutation of it — and no structure was deposited (DCAF16 entry count unchanged at 3). 'There are more DCAF16 binders' was never the blocker. The FEM1B paper is a different question entirely — see TRG-FEM1B-LINKER-BEARING-STRUCTURE.

triggers.consequence_caveat: ⚠ A HIT ON THIS TRIGGER DOES NOT BY ITSELF RESTART ANY WORK, and saying so is not a demotion of the trigger — it is the thing a reader needs in order to act on a hit correctly. R9 and R12 are both 'future — NOT STARTED', and emc-post-degrader-options.md section 0 puts the E3 recruiter on the LIABILITY side of the split it draws ('the degradation geometry — ternary, E3, exit vector, ubiquitin transfer, and a ~1 kcal/mol paralogue margin'), not on the ASSET side. So a partner-free liganded structure reopens a parked row inside a programme that is parked for unrelated, architectural reasons. It would still be a real field advance and worth recording; it would not be a reason to spend.

triggers.title: A deposited FEM1B structure carrying a linker-bearing (>=500 Da) ligand
triggers.capability: FEM1B is NOT one of the blocked recruiters — it PASSED all three gates of the 2026-07-25 downselect (G1 on 9PW8 @ 2.8 A, ligand A1CLY; G2 buried fraction 0.8694; G3 clearance 25.0 A, 30-degree cone openness 0.5429) and already has 7 partner-free liganded entries (geometry_frame.n_clean_binary_entries = 7: 9PQ9/9PQA/9PQE/9PW8/9PWJ/9PXO/9PXP, all released 2025-11-26, from the Protein Sci NMR fragment screen PMID 41229306). It was dropped on the PARETO front, at linker_analogue_tier 1 and open_solid_angle_fraction_15A 0.0449 — the tightest exit in the panel. The capability watched here is the one that would move the FIRST of those two: a deposited entry in which FEM1B is bound by a >=500 Da ligand, which is what tier 1 records as absent.
triggers._why_separate_from_TRG-E3-RECRUITER-STRU: Different criterion, different consequence. That trigger asks whether a site survives partner removal; FEM1B's already does. This one asks whether the exit vector has been SHOWN to tolerate a linker. Merging them would let a FEM1B hit read as a DCAF16 unblocking, which is exactly the conflation the 2026-08-03 grading had to undo.

evidence_home.note: section 5 dropped-set table (FEM1B row) and section 8, which states the limit this trigger watches: 'A tier-1 recruiter is "no solved linker-bearing structure", not "no linker chemistry exists".'

decisive_evidence.check: RCSB search on Q9UK73, newest first; then e3-recruiter-staging.json FEM1B.linker_bearing_analogue.n_entries_with_ligand_ge_500Da.
decisive_evidence.baseline_2026_08_03: 31 entries, newest release 2025-11-26 (the VU-series fragment structures). n_entries_with_ligand_ge_500Da = 0.

reopens.note: ⚠ Clearing tier 1 would NOT by itself advance FEM1B. It lost on TWO Pareto axes and the second, open_solid_angle_fraction_15A = 0.0449, is untouched by any amount of linker chemistry — only a new conformer, re-measured, could move it. So a hit here licenses a $0 re-run of the downselect, nothing more. The consequence_caveat on TRG-E3-RECRUITER-STRUCTURE applies here in full.

last_graded.why: The paper reports FEM1B-based PROTACs on a dual-site ligand FL47 — i.e. exactly the linker chemistry that section 8's limit anticipated — but it deposited nothing: FEM1B's newest released entry is still 2025-11-26 and is cited to Protein Sci., not to this paper. The structurally-defined tier therefore cannot move. ⚠ PROVISIONAL on the paper: it is paywalled and only the ABSTRACT was obtained, and an abstract cannot establish a buried fraction or an exit vector.

triggers.on_fire: Re-run e3_recruiter_staging.py with the new entry in scope and read the Pareto front again. Do not report FEM1B as advanced on the tier alone — check the openness axis.

triggers.capability: A molecular glue whose selectivity was PREDICTED before it was found, or a predictor scored on held-out glue interfaces. The program's own thesis is that in every landmark case glue selectivity was discovered and then rationalised by a solved ternary, never predicted blind.

triggers.on_fire: Re-grade route 10 from 'watch, do not build'. A retrospective rationalisation of a found glue does NOT fire this trigger; the test is prospective.
